text: Standstill agreements defraud shareholders who are not parties to them in two distinct ways: by violating the shareholder's right to the best available merger or transaction and by discouraging unsolicited tender offers in which a significant control premium could be realized.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3017612

isBasedOn.name: Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America

abstract: standstill agreements defraud shareholders not privy to the agreement in two ways: (1) by violating a shareholder's right to the best available merger or transaction, and (2) by discouraging unsolicited tender offers where a significant control premium can be realized.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: standstill agreements binding only some shareholders
applying the Schreiber v. Carney definition of fraud
